rounds.text: Majestic Auto Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a steep discount with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.57x against a sector benchmark of 1.42x [E2, E7]. This asset-level discount is staggering when considering that the company's market value of investments alone stands at Rs. 418 Cr., which comfortably exceeds the total market capitalization of Rs. 380 Cr. [E3, E62]. Furthermore, the business is practically debt-free, having dramatically reduced its borrowings from Rs. 145 Cr. to just Rs. 15 Cr. in March 2026, supported by a comfortable current ratio of 33.29x [E37, E38, E39, E59]. Shareholders are also well-compensated while waiting for the market to rerate the stock, enjoying a robust dividend yield of 6.85% backed by a healthy dividend payout of 89.8% [E4, E63]. Intrinsic valuation models underscore this mispricing, with a discounted cash flow analysis indicating an intrinsic value of Rs. 1188 per share, creating a substantial margin of safety of 69.3% [E45, E46]. Conceded: the company has suffered from poor historical sales growth, including a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of -13% and an operating margin that has trended downward over the last four years [E14, E31, E64].

Majestic Auto Ltd suffers from severe top-line erosion, evidenced by a compounded sales growth rate of -13% over 10 years, -9% over 5 years, -11% over 3 years, and a catastrophic -69% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15, E16, E17]. This top-line collapse directly impacts operating efficiency, as the operating margin has plummeted by 103 percentage points to -38% in the TTM compared to 65% three years earlier, with both yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends reading as decreasing [E30, E31, E32]. Furthermore, core operational profitability fails to generate actual liquidity, demonstrated by a negative operating cash flow of Rs -7 Cr and a negative free cash flow of Rs -19 Cr in March 2026, leading to a weak cash conversion ratio of -0.08x [E33, E34, E35]. Capital efficiency remains deeply depressed, with a 10-year median ROE of just 2%, a 3-year median ROE of 3%, and a TTM ROE lagging the sector benchmark at 3.33% versus 5.08% [E9, E26, E28]. Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.02x with borrowings reduced to Rs 15 Cr, and its market value of investments exceeds its market capitalization [E37, E39, E62]. However, reported earnings are heavily inflated by non-operating sources, specifically including Rs 151 Cr of other income [E66].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over 10, 5, and 3 years, as well as the TTM period, shows negative percentages [E14, E15, E16, E17], and operating margins have decreased [E30, E31, E32]. However, the top-line decline misses the extraordinary asset protection and hidden value present in the balance sheet, where the market value of investments alone at Rs. 418 Cr exceeds the total market capitalization of Rs. 380 Cr [E62]. Conceded: operating cash flow and free cash flow for March 2026 are negative [E34, E35]. Yet the bear's panic over cash is completely neutralized by a massive current ratio of 33.29x and borrowings dropping drastically from Rs 145 Cr to just Rs 15 Cr, leaving the company almost debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.02x [E37, E38, E39, E59]. Furthermore, while the bear decries low ROE [E9, E26, E28], it ignores a stellar return on assets of 13.95% that soundly beats the sector benchmark of 2.86% [E8], alongside a robust 6.85% dividend yield supported by a healthy 89.8% payout [E4, E63]. Finally, the market price of Rs 365 sits at a staggering 0.57x price-to-book ratio and a bargain EV/EBITDA of 2.11x versus a sector benchmark of 10.61x, completely pricing in any operational headwinds [E2, E7, E11, E60].

Conceded: the market value of investments stands at Rs. 418 Cr against a market capitalization of Rs. 380 Cr [E62]. However, the bull's reliance on asset protection and investments ignores that reported earnings are heavily distorted by non-operating gains, specifically including an other income of Rs. 151 Cr [E66]. Conceded: borrowings dropped to Rs. 15 Cr and the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.02x [E37, E39]. Yet this balance-sheet comfort is severely undermined by negative operating cash flow of Rs -7 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -19 Cr for March 2026 [E34, E35], alongside a cash conversion ratio of -0.08x [E33]. Conceded: ROA reaches 13.95% [E8] and the dividend yield is 6.85% [E4]. Nonetheless, these metrics mask a deeply impaired core business carrying a multi-year top-line collapse, evidenced by compounded sales growth of -13% over 10 years, -9% over 5 years, -11% over 3 years, and -69% in the trailing twelve months [E14, E15, E16, E17], driven by operating margins plunging by -103 percentage points down to -38% in the TTM period [E30].
